title: Recover worker event log wake signals with setup
instructions:
Recover from failed run runs/2026-06-07T05-27-58-735Z-worker-event-log-wake-signal.json. That run ended blocked because the isolated worktree did not have installed dependencies, so do not treat its dirty worktree output as trusted completion. Use the failed run log only as evidence of the environment blocker and the original task intent.

Implement a local Samantha-owned append-only JSONL event log for worker wake signals. The goal is to reduce token-heavy supervision polling by letting an operator wait on small run events instead of repeatedly reading worker thread context.

Required behavior:
- Add a focused src/core/run-events.ts module for writing and reading run events under a runs directory, defaulting to events.jsonl.
- Define closed event shapes for at least worker_turn_completed and worker_run_log_written.
- Event records must include schemaVersion, eventId, eventType, runId, taskId, createdAt, and enough small evidence fields to wake supervision without reading thread context. worker_run_log_written must include runLogPath, pass, and HARNESS_RESULT status when available.
- Treat events as advisory wake signals only. They must not accept, merge, clean, commit, push, mutate lifecycle state, rewrite policy, or replace HARNESS_RESULT, scope checks, deterministic verification, run logs, run index, or Samantha-owned lifecycle evidence.
- Emit worker_turn_completed from the worker dispatch path only after the worker runtime returns. Do not emit it for setup failure or pre-runtime dispatch blocks.
- Emit worker_run_log_written from run-task only after writeWorkerRunLog and RunIndex.append have completed.
- Add a narrow explicit CLI read/wait surface. Prefer names such as runs:events for reading recent events and runs:wait for waiting for one event. The wait command must be bounded by a timeout and must only inspect the local event log or filesystem state, not worker thread context.
- Keep the CLI local-only. Do not add a daemon, background service, remote adapter, dashboard, routine trigger, connector, hidden memory, worker-owned event trust, automatic accept, automatic merge, automatic cleanup, automatic commit, automatic push, or continuation successor execution.

Implementation guidance:
- The setup command installs dependencies in the isolated worktree before worker dispatch. Do not edit package.json or bun.lock.
- Use append-only JSONL with deterministic parsing behavior. Ignore or report malformed lines in a diagnosable way without trusting them.
- Keep polling inside runs:wait cheap and bounded if direct file watch is not used. A small interval is acceptable because it reads only events.jsonl, not large thread context.
- Reuse existing styles in src/cli.ts, tests/cli.test.ts, and tests/worker-dispatch.test.ts.
- If executeWorkerDispatch needs an injected event callback to emit worker_turn_completed at the right boundary, keep it narrow and optional.

Required tests:
- Focused run-events tests prove append/read behavior, event filtering by type/task/run id, timeout behavior, and malformed-line handling if implemented.
- Worker dispatch tests prove worker_turn_completed is emitted after a successful runtime return and is not emitted when setup fails before runtime dispatch.
- CLI tests prove parser coverage for the new read/wait commands, successful wait/read output from a temp runs directory, timeout behavior, and no mutation outside the event log.
- Existing codex-sdk runtime and run-task behavior must continue to pass.

Stop conditions:
- Stop and report rework if setup still cannot install dependencies in the isolated worktree.
- Stop and report rework if implementing this requires daemon/background operation, remote/control-plane integration, dashboards, routine triggers, worker-owned orchestration, worker-owned trusted completion, or automatic lifecycle mutation.
- Stop and report rework if event receipt would become a trusted gate or would bypass HARNESS_RESULT parsing, changed-file scope checks, deterministic verification, run log writing, run index writing, or Samantha-owned accept/merge/cleanup authority.
- Stop and report rework if the implementation requires changing TaskSpec contracts, dispatch policy, merge/accept/cleanup logic, batch execution, sequential continuation automation, package metadata, or doctrine documents.

End with exactly one HARNESS_RESULT line.
